 Dated this the 12th day of December, 2012  J U D G M E N T K.M.Joseph, J.
Petitioner has approached this Court seeking the following reliefs.

"(i) issue a Writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate Writ, Order or Direction,
directing the respondents 1 to 3 to provide adequate and effective protection to the life of the petitioner and his workers engaged in his Vegetable Shop viz. C.T.N.
Vegetables, Near Government Model High School, Varkala, Thiruvananthapuram C. Thankappan vs The Director General Of Police on 2 May, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8071749/
3 District and also for the smooth functioning of his business forthwith.

(ii) issue a Writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate Writ, Order or Direction,
directing the 10th respondent to take immediate action against the respondents 4 to 9 for their illegal demand of Nokkukooli from the petitioner, in the light of Exhibit P-5 Circular forthwith."
2. Briefly put the case of the petitioner is as follows.

The petitioner is a senior citizen of India, who is conducting wholesale and retail vegetable business under the name and style of 'C.T.N.Vegetables'
near Government Higher Secondary School, Temple Road, Varkala at his 18 Cents of property comprised in Survey No.1011/7 of Varkala Village, after obtaining necessary licenses as evidenced by Exts. P1 to P4.

The petitioner employed three permanent workers for loading and unloading works in his shop, since the loading and unloading of the articles in the petitioner's business required special care and caution of the experienced hands.

But the respondents 4 to 9 who are the head load workers of INTUC Trade Union of the Ruling party, unnecessarily created problems due to non-payment of 'Nokkukooli' which was banned as per Ext. P5 circular of the 1st respondent.
When the petitioner stopped the payment of Nokkukooli, they created unwanted problems and even attacked the petitioner's workers, as evidenced by Ext.P7.

Though the petitioner filed various complaints before the police, 10th respondent and also other higher authorities seeking protection of his life and property, nobody had taken any action for redressing his grievance, due to the political interference of the Ruling Party and hence this writ petition.
3. We have heard the Learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader.
4. The area where the shop is situated, is apparently covered by the scheme.
The petitioner does not have a case, otherwise.
If that be so, the petitioner's workers who are not registered under the 'Head Load Workers Act', cannot possibly provide the answer to the question raised in the writ petition.
The loading and unloading work can be done in the scheme area only through registered workers.
It may be true that the applications are pending.
Unless the petitioner has registered workers, the loading and unloading work shall be done through the pool workers.
In such circumstances, we are not inclined to interfere in the matter.
The writ petition is closed.

Sd/-
K.M.JOSEPH, JUDGE Sd/-
